descriptionChirho: A visible mark or brand stamped or imprinted on the body as a sign of ownership or allegiance; used exclusively in Revelation for the 'mark of the beast' imposed on the right hand or forehead as a prerequisite for commerce (Rev 13:16-17, 14:9, 14:11, 15:2, 16:2, 19:20, 20:4). Spanish 'marca', Arabic 'سِمَة', Korean '표', Swahili 'chapa', Hindi 'चिह्न' all denote an impressed stamp or brand mark.

Something formed by artistic carving, engraving, or sculpting; used in Acts 17:29 where Paul argues that the divine nature should not be thought of as something like gold, silver, or stone shaped by human art and imagination — an engraved or sculpted representation. Arabic 'نَقش' (engraving), Swahili 'sanamu iliyochongwa' (carved idol/image), Korean '조각된 것' (sculpted thing), Hindi 'नक्काशी' (carving), Spanish 'grabado' (engraving) all distinguish this as artistic craftsmanship rather than a stamped brand.
